subject: Re: repeated sampling in a season

messages.author: 05dddafe48e2273c
messages.subject: repeated sampling in a season
parts:
I conducted point count surveys this past year for a target species. I
surveyed each point twice within the breeding season (one round completed in
April and the other in May). Do I need to account for this in the survey
effort - i.e. should I use the multiplier option to divide the density
estimate by the effort (which would be 2)? I have not been able to find a
clear answer in the distance smapling books or other papers.

Thanks for any assistance,

Jennifer Reidy
jennife...@gmail.com

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: repeated sampling in a season
parts:
Yes - if you just want to pool April and May data to increase sample
size, then record all detections for each point, regardless of which
visit the detection was made, then either record effort for each point
as 2 or add an overall multiplier (or rather 'divider') of 2. (The
former approach is usually preferred, in case not all points were
visited the same number of times.)

Steve Buckland
